agent: savegame wave, reader C (the unit tree and the country's military blocks)
question: How the original writes and reads the military part of a save: every unit level, brigade, order and mission, the active leaders, the production and deployment lines and the saved templates - key order, keys written only sometimes, how each is read back and what AfterLoad fills in.

addresses.name: CUnit::SaveContents
addresses.comment: **The common body of every unit block in a save**, slot 2 of the CPersistent table CUnit keeps at +8 - so `this` here is the unit + 8, and every offset below is the unit's own (the code's + 8). 0x5B8170 to the `ret 4` at 0x5B8C50. First it sets the unit's +0x49 (saved_this_pass). Then, in this order: `id` (the {id type} pair at +0x10, always); `name` (+0x16C, always, quoted); `base` = the base province's id, only where home_base_ptr (+0x98) is set and its slot 1 (IsCarrier) answers false - so an air group on a carrier and every land unit write none; `leader` {id type} where the leader (+0x12C) answers true to its slot 8 (CNullLeader answers false); `previous` (+0x134) where set; `movement_progress` (+0x14C, fixed, always); `arrow_state` (+0x18C) where not 0; `path` (the CList of province ids at +0x138, through SaveWriteIntList - nothing when empty); `location` (+0x130) where set; `retreat=yes` where +0x158 is set; `dig_in` (+0x1C8), `attack_delay` (+0xD4) and `combat_hours` (+0xD8), each only where above 0; `is_prioritized` (+0xA4), `can_reinforce` (+0xA6), `can_upgrade` (+0xA5) as yes/no and `fuel` (+0x100), `supplies` (+0xFC) as fixed, all five always. Then every brigade of +0x38 under `regiment`, `ship` or `wing` by its slots 9/10/11 (a sub unit answering none of them is not written), each by its own Save. Then the children (+0x1E4) in list order: one whose +0x49 is already set is skipped; an air unit whose base answers IsCarrier is skipped (its ship writes it); a land child carried by a fleet (CArmy +0x300) or by air (+0x304) is skipped too, because its carrier writes it - **except** that where the carrying fleet is the child itself or lies in the child's own subtree (CUnit::HasDescendant), the fleet is written here, under `navy`, in the child's place; every other child goes under the key of its oob_level (+0x1F4: theatre, armygroup, army, corps, division, navy, air; `none` for any other), written by its CPersistent Save. Then the order (+0xB0) under its own key (slot 16, GetTypeId) where its slot 24 answers true - every order class but CNullOrder. Then `start_date` (+0xCC) and `end_date` (+0xD0) as date strings, each only where its year is above 1 (not the null date); `disengage` (+0xA8) and `possible_retreat` (+0xAC) together, where disengage is above 0; `track=yes` where +0x95 (shadowed_by_patrol) is set; `was_paradropped=yes` where +0x97 is set; `plan` = the CUnitPlan at +0x1FC through its slot 1, where plan_active (+0x204) is set and oob_level is below 4; `expeditionary_owner` (the tag, quoted) and `expeditionary_date` where +0x290 is not 0; `aggression_enabled=yes` and `aggression_setting` (+0x4C, fixed) where +0x4A is set; and `country_intel`, the 12-byte entries of +0x2A8..+0x2AC flattened into one vector of ints (0x4608D0), where there are any. `is_reserve` is never written though CUnit::LoadKey reads it. Callers: CArmy::SaveContents, CNavy::SaveContents and CAir::SaveContents first thing, and this table's own slot 2.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing, 0x5B8170-0x5B8C50; every key token named through ghidra/saveTokens.json; the jump table at 0x5B8C54 holds the seven level arms 0x5B86C1-0x5B8745. `this` = unit + 8 checked by is_prioritized at [ebx+0x9C] = CUnit +0xA4, fuel [ebx+0xF8] = +0x100, leader [ebx+0x124] = +0x12C, all recorded fields. Against seven saves (the 1, 4, 7 and 8 January 1936 ones, 2 September 1936, Ireland August 1938): 14,007 unit blocks of every level follow exactly this order, `base` only on air and navy, `plan` only on theatres, `parent` only on a division carried by a fleet, and every carrier air group (98 in four saves) sits inside its `ship` with no `base`. Wrong if a unit block were found with `path` after `location`, or a carrier air group at theatre level.

addresses.name: CAir::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CAir's CPersistent table (at +8, so `this` is the air unit + 8): CUnit::SaveContents, then **every land unit the air unit carries** (its list at +0x2E4, the one CAir::Board fills) each under the key of its oob_level (theatre .. air, `none` for any other) and written by its own Save - the air-transport mirror of CNavy::SaveContents, with no `at_sea` after it. 0x5D06B0 to the `ret 4` at 0x5D0740. No save of the maintainer's has a land unit inside an `air` block.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x5D06B0-0x5D0740: call 0x5B8170, then the loop over [esi+0x2DC] (air + 0x2E4) with the jump table at 0x5D0744 of seven arms and the 0x18D default, and the carried unit's slot 1 through its +8 subobject. The seven-save census finds no land block inside an air block. Wrong if the list at +0x2E4 on a CAir held anything but land units.

addresses.name: CSubUnit::SaveContents
addresses.comment: **What a `regiment`, `ship` or `wing` block holds**, slot 2 of CSubUnit, CRegiment and CWing (CShip adds to it). In order: `id` {id type} (+0x8/+0xC); `name` (+0x68, always); `home` (+0x64's province id) where set; `type` (the definition's name, +0x58); `organisation` (+0x60), `strength` (+0x5C), `highest` (+0x30, strength_ceiling) and `experience` (+0x3C), fixed, always; `is_reserve=yes` (+0xA4) and `pride=yes` (+0xA5) only where set; `current_distance` (+0xC8, fixed) only where the brigade's unit (+0xB0) is in a battle (its +0x11C combats_count above 0); `builder` (the tag at +0x34, quoted) where its id half (+0x38) is not 0; `sunk_by` {id type} (+0x9C/+0xA0) where not the game's no-object pair; and then one line per node of the technology list +0x84, `<technology>={<level> <progress>}`. **`historical_model` is never written**, though CSubUnit::LoadKey reads it - so every brigade loaded from a save has -1 there and CSubUnit::AfterLoad skips its model steps. 0x5A92A0 to the `ret 4` at 0x5A98F5.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing; tokens through saveTokens.json; the current_distance gate at 0x5A94E1-0x5A94F2 and the builder gate at 0x5A9513. The census over seven saves: 23,678 regiment, 4,715 ship and 1,032 wing blocks, every one in this order (`id name [home] type organisation strength highest experience [is_reserve] [pride] [current_distance] [builder] <technologies>`), `current_distance` on 15 only, and no `historical_model` anywhere in the 45 saves. Wrong if a sub unit block were found with the technologies before `builder`.

addresses.name: CShip::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CShip: CSubUnit::SaveContents, then `air` once for each air unit in the carrier's list at +0xDC, written by the air unit's own Save (its +8 subobject's slot 1). **This is the only place a carrier's air group is written**: CUnit::SaveContents and CCountry::SaveContents both skip an air unit whose base answers IsCarrier. 0x5ADD30 to the `ret 4` at 0x5ADD7D. Read back by CShip::LoadKey's one case, `air`.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x5ADD30-0x5ADD7D: call 0x5A92A0, the loop over [esi+0xDC] with SaveWriteKey(0x440) and slot 1. In four saves 98 air blocks sit inside ship blocks, all without `base`, and every other air block has one. Wrong if a carrier group were found written at its theatre as well.

addresses.name: CLeader::SaveContents
addresses.comment: **All a save keeps of a leader**, slot 2 of CLeader and CNullLeader, written inside the country's `active_leaders` block. In order: `rank` (+0x6C, always); `skill` (+0x70) **only where it differs from starting_skill (+0xC8)**; `current_experience` (+0x78, the 64-bit value) as a token of type 0x18F - 15 fractional bits, printed `2000.00000` in a text save and as the raw `%lld` in a binary one; `gainable_trait` = the CTraitGainTracker (+0xC4) through its own Save, where there is one; and `trait = { ... }`, the names of the trait list (+0x30), where its count (+0x38) is above 0. Nothing else: not the name, country, type, picture, loyalty, max skill or history - a leader's definition comes back from history/leaders, and **only the leaders in service are written at all**. 0x57FDB0 to the `ret 4` at 0x57FF59.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing: rank at 0x57FDD9, the skill test against [edi+0xC8] at 0x57FE1A, the '%lld' format and the 0xC/0x18F type choice on writer +0xC at 0x57FE68-0x57FE98, the tracker at 0x57FEB5, the trait list at 0x57FED8. Census: 24,441 active leader entries in seven saves, keys `rank [skill] current_experience gainable_trait [trait]` only, `skill` on 218. Wrong if a save's active leader were found with `name` or `history`.

addresses.name: COrder::SaveContents
addresses.comment: **The common body of every order in a save**, slot 2 of COrder, CNullOrder, CMoveOrder and CStrategicRedeploymentOrder and the first call of every other order's writer. In order: `province` (+0xC's id) where set; `target` {id type} (+0x10/+0x14) where it is not the game's no-object pair (the globals 0x1A8CC94/0x1A8CC98); `stance` (+0x20); `start_date` (+0x28) and `death_date` (+0x2C) as date strings, both always; `return_to_base` (+0x18) yes/no; `time` (+0x30); `priority` (+0x1C); `stop` (+0x24, fixed). 0x587530 to the `ret 4` at 0x5877DA. The unit writes the block under the order's own key (its slot 16) and only for an order whose slot 24 answers true, which is every class but CNullOrder.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x587530-0x5877DA. Every strategic_redeployment (606) and support_attack block in the seven-save census is `province stance start_date death_date return_to_base time priority stop`, and every naval and air order begins the same way. Wrong if `target` were found written as {0 0} - it is skipped for the null pair.

addresses.name: CNavalOrder::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CNavalOrder and the first call of every naval order's writer: COrder::SaveContents, then **CNavalOrder's own** `return_to_base` (+0x34) and `priority` (+0x38), then `capital` (+0x3C), `sub_unit` (+0x40) and `other` (+0x44), all always. So every naval order in a save carries `return_to_base` and `priority` twice, and since CNavalOrder::LoadKey takes both keys into +0x34/+0x38 both times, COrder's +0x18 and +0x1C are never set from a save. 0x59AEE0 to the `ret 4` at 0x59B05F.
addresses.evidence: Read whole; call 0x587530 then the five keys off [edi+0x34..0x44]. Every patrol, rebase, transport, convoy_raid and join_fleet block in the census has the pair twice and `capital sub_unit other` after it. Wrong if a naval order block were found with a single `priority`.

addresses.name: CRebaseOrder::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CRebaseOrder, CReserveOrder and CNavalTransportOrder - the three siblings that also share CRebaseOrder::LoadKey - and nothing but a tail `jmp CNavalOrder::SaveContents` (0x59B620, five bytes). So `rebase`, `reserves` and `transport` blocks are a plain naval order.
addresses.evidence: 0x59B620 decodes as `jmp 0x59AEE0` at its entry; vtable.py --holding 0x59B620 gives exactly these three tables, all CNavalOrder heirs. Census: rebase (15) and transport (6) blocks end at `other`.

addresses.name: CPatrolOrder::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CPatrolOrder: CNavalOrder::SaveContents, then **`provinces` = an {id type} block** - the id pair at +0x4C/+0x50 of the reference whose pointer is at +0x48, the fleet the patrol is shadowing - written always, `{ id=0 type=0 }` when there is none, and followed by an empty line. The key says provinces and holds a unit reference; CPatrolOrder::LoadKey reads it back through ParseObjectReference into +0x48. 0x59C9F0 to the `ret 4` at 0x59CA3A.
addresses.evidence: Read whole: SaveWriteKey(0x1DC) and the id writer on [esi+0x4C]/[esi+0x50] with no branch. All 49 patrol blocks in the census end in `provinces = { id=0 type=0 }` and a blank line. CPatrolOrder::LoadKey (0x59C9C0) puts the same key through ParseObjectReference at this+0x48. Wrong if a patrol were found with a province list under the key.

addresses.name: CConvoyRaid::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CConvoyRaid: CNavalOrder::SaveContents, then `attack` = the int at +0x4C as `%d`, always. 0x5A0320 to the `ret 4` at 0x5A037F. The census values run 2 to 12. Read back by CConvoyRaid::LoadKey's one case.
addresses.evidence: Read whole: call 0x59AEE0, mov edi,[edi+0x4C], SaveWriteKey(0x174), sprintf '%d' type 0xC. Eight convoy_raid blocks in the census end in `attack=N`.

addresses.name: CConvoyEscortOrder::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CConvoyEscortOrder: CNavalOrder::SaveContents, then `province` (the int at +0x70), `direction` (the byte at +0x7C, yes/no) and `convoy` {id type} (+0x4C/+0x50), all always. 0x59FD70 to the `ret 4` at 0x59FE49. The loader's three cases are the same keys. No save of the maintainer's has a convoy_escort.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing; tokens 0x1EE, 0x4C, 0x4D8. Not seen in a save, so the field meanings rest on the key names only.

addresses.name: CNavalInterceptOrder::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CNavalInterceptOrder: CNavalOrder::SaveContents, then it resolves the target id pair (+0x4C/+0x50) with FindPersistentById, caches the answer at +0x48 - so writing the order also refreshes it - and writes `provinces` {id type} **only where it resolves**. Read back by CPatrolOrder::LoadKey, which it inherits. 0x59E130 to the `ret 4` at 0x59E1BA. No save of the maintainer's has an `intercept`.
addresses.evidence: Read whole: the FindPersistentById call at 0x59E16F, the store at 0x59E17F, the skip at 0x59E184. Slot 4 of the table is 0x59C9C0, CPatrolOrder::LoadKey.

addresses.name: CNavalSortieOrder::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CNavalSortieOrder: CNavalOrder::SaveContents, then `start` (the id of the province at +0x48), one `provinces = <id>` line per node of the list at +0x50, and `current` (the id of the province at +0x4C). 0x59E920 to the `ret 4` at 0x59EB01. The loader's three cases are the same keys. No save of the maintainer's has a sortie.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing; tokens 0x68, 0x1DC, 0x628, each value through TokenText.

addresses.name: CJoinFleetOrder::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CJoinFleetOrder: CNavalOrder::SaveContents, then `join_fleet` {id type} of the fleet to join (+0x48/+0x4C), always - read back by CJoinFleetOrder::LoadKey through ParseObjectId into +0x48. The `target` COrder writes before it is a separate pair. 0x59BF70 to the `ret 4` at 0x59BF98.
addresses.evidence: Read whole: lea eax,[esi+0x48] into the id writer. Ten join_fleet blocks in the census end in a `join_fleet = { id type }` block, with a `target` block earlier.

addresses.name: CAirOrder::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CAirOrder and of 13 of its subclasses, and the first call of every other air order's writer: COrder::SaveContents, then **`return_to_base` (+0x18) and `priority` (+0x1C) a second time** - the same fields again, not copies of their own; then one `provinces = <id>` line per node of the area list at +0x44; then, for every sub unit definition whose is_air (+0x2C) is set, `<type name> = by_unit_type[type_index] * 1000` written as fixed (SaveWriteNamedFixed) - so the line reads `interceptor=0.000` for 0, and CAirOrder::LoadKey's `%i` reads `N.000` back as N. The sub unit database is fetched with an inlined lazy getter. 0x589CD0 to the `ret 4` at 0x58A08C.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing: the duplicate keys at 0x589D03/0x589D5B off [esi+0x18]/[esi+0x1C], the province loop at 0x589DA1, the `imul eax, eax, 0x3E8` at 0x589E99, the is_air test at 0x589F72 and the name at definition +8 (0x58A054). In the 45 saves all 824 such lines read 0.000, and every air order block carries eleven of them - the eleven air types of the base game. Wrong if a non-zero line were ever seen with decimals.

addresses.name: CAirReserveOrder::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CAirReserveOrder: a tail `jmp CAirOrder::SaveContents`, nothing more.
addresses.evidence: 0x5964A0 decodes as `jmp 0x589CD0`; one table holds it.

addresses.name: CJoinAirOrder::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CJoinAirOrder: CAirOrder::SaveContents, then `target` {id type} of the air unit to join (+0x84/+0x88), always - a **second** `target` key where COrder's own was not the null pair. CJoinAirOrder::LoadKey takes every `target` into its reference at +0x80, so COrder's +0x10/+0x14 are never set from a save on this order. 0x597E30 to the `ret 4` at 0x597E80.
addresses.evidence: Read whole; CJoinAirOrder::LoadKey (0x597E00) compares 0x6A and calls ParseObjectReference with esi = this+0x80. Not seen in a save.

addresses.name: CRebaseToCarrierMission::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CRebaseToCarrierMission: CAirOrder::SaveContents, then `carrier_target` {id type} (+0x84/+0x88, the carrier's fleet), always. 0x593A80 to the `ret 4` at 0x593AD0.
addresses.evidence: Read whole; token 0x576; the pair is the record's carrier_fleet_type/carrier_fleet_id.

addresses.name: CParadropMission::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CParadropMission, and **the one order writer that writes its own key first**: `message` (+0x80, yes/no) and only then CAirOrder::SaveContents. 0x590880 to the `ret 4` at 0x5908F4.
addresses.evidence: Read whole: SaveWriteKey(0xE1) at 0x59089D precedes the call 0x589CD0 at 0x5908E9.

addresses.name: CNukeMission::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CNukeMission: CAirOrder::SaveContents, then `nukes` (the int at +0x80), always. 0x595240 to the `ret 4` at 0x5952A2.
addresses.evidence: Read whole; token 0x577.

addresses.name: CTransportSuppliesOrder::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CTransportSuppliesOrder: CAirOrder::SaveContents, then `supplies` (+0x84) and `fuel` (+0x80), fixed, always - the cargo aboard. 0x5953A0 to the `ret 4` at 0x595474.
addresses.evidence: Read whole; tokens 0x469 and 0x46C off [ebx+0x84] and [ebx+0x80], the record's cargo_supplies and cargo_fuel.

addresses.name: CUnitPlan::SaveContents
addresses.comment: **A unit's `plan` block**, slot 2 of CUnitPlan. In order: `active` (+0x8, yes/no); `allow_hq_reorg=yes` (+0x9) only where set; `stance` (+0xC), `air_stance` (+0x10), `naval_stance` (+0x14); `path` (+0x48) and `path2` (+0x5C) through SaveWriteIntList, so only where not empty; `our_power` (+0x80) and `their_power` (+0x84), fixed; `embark` (+0x88) and `debark` (+0x8C); `ops_area` = the province ids of the list at +0x18 as a vector, only where there are any; `fallback_line` = another province vector, from the list at +0x28; one `objective` block per node of +0x38 by the objective's own Save (`province`, `priority`); and `min` = the vector at +0x70, where it is not empty. 0x8DF160 to the `ret 4` at 0x8DF714. CUnit::SaveContents writes it only where the plan is active and the unit is a corps or above.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing for the key order and gates (tokens 0x50A, 0x73F, 0x124, 0x73D, 0x73E, 0x19C, 0x6F4, 0x72E, 0x72F, 0x731, 0x732, 0x6F3, 0x74C, 0x714, 0x719); the two province-list-to-vector copies between them were not followed instruction by instruction. Census: 639 plan blocks, all `active stance air_stance naval_stance [path] our_power their_power embark debark [ops_area] [objective] min`, all on theatres; fallback_line and path2 never seen.

addresses.name: CMilitaryConstruction::SaveContents
addresses.comment: **A `military_construction` line**, slot 2: CConstruction::SaveContents (`id size cost duration progress status [location] [country] [builder]`), then `name` (+0x60) **only where its length (+0x70) is above 1**; `unit` {id type} (+0x58/+0x5C), always; `manpower` (+0x98, fixed), always; `target` {id type} (+0x90/+0x94) where not 0/0; `is_reserve=yes` (+0x8C) and `factor` (+0x9C, fixed) **together, only where is_reserve is set**; then every brigade of the list at +0x7C as `<sub unit type> = { ... }` written by the brigade definition's own Save; then `accumulated_experiance` (+0xA4) and `accumulated_progress` (+0xA8), fixed, always. 0x4843F0 to the `ret 4` at 0x4846C6.
addresses.evidence: Read whole; the name gate `cmp [edi+0x70], 1 / jle` at 0x484423 (the std::string size beside the buffer at +0x60), the is_reserve gate at 0x4844D7 covering both keys. Census of 651 lines: `name` on 290, `is_reserve` and `factor` on the same 227, the brigade blocks between `manpower`/`factor` and `accumulated_experiance`.

addresses.name: CBrigadeConstructionDefinition::SaveContents
addresses.comment: One brigade of a military line, written under its sub unit type's name: `id` {id type} (+0x10/+0x14); `name` (+0x18) where not empty; `model` = the int list at +0x44 through SaveWriteIntList; `experience` (+0x40, fixed) where not 0; `upgrading_from_subunit` (the name of the definition at +0x38) where set; and `upgrading_from_subunit_str` (+0x3C, fixed) where not 0. Never `historical_model`, which its loader also takes. 0x483080 to the `ret 4` at 0x483115.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing; tokens 0xB, 0x1A, 0x45C, 0x48B, 0x7CE, 0x7CF. Census: every one of the 1,400 brigade blocks in seven saves is `id name model`; the upgrade keys were not seen.

addresses.name: CUnitDeployment::SaveContents
addresses.comment: **A `unit_deployment` entry** - a finished unit not yet placed: `id` {id type}, then the one unit at +0x38 under the key its kind gives - CUnit_SaveTokenForOobLevel for a land unit (slot 15), `navy` (slot 16) or `air` (slot 17), nothing for any other - written by the unit's own Save. The unit has no `location`. 0x57E3C0 to the `ret 4` at 0x57E417 (a second exit at 0x57E476).
addresses.evidence: Read whole. Census: 12 unit_deployment blocks, each `id` and one unit (8 air, 3 navy, 1 division), and those twelve are exactly the unit blocks in the seven saves with no `location`.

addresses.name: CUnitDeployment::GetType
addresses.comment: Slot 8 of CUnitDeployment, `mov eax, 0x4B4; ret`: the save token `unit_deployment`, the key CCountry::SaveContents writes the entry under. CBuildingDeployment::GetType is the same with 0x4B7, `building_deployment`.
addresses.evidence: Six bytes at 0x482A30; one table holds it; called through slot 8 at 0x4D1594 in CCountry::SaveContents' deployment loop, whose key it becomes.

addresses.name: CBuildingDeployment::SaveContents
addresses.comment: **A `building_deployment` entry** - a finished building with no province yet: `id` {id type}, then `building` = the building's index (+0x38's +0x54). 0x57EEA0 to the `ret 4` at 0x57EF11.
addresses.evidence: Read whole; tokens 0xB and 0x1FE. Not seen in a save of the maintainer's.

addresses.name: CDivisionTemplate::Save
addresses.comment: **CDivisionTemplate overrides CPersistent's Save itself** (slot 1; its slot 2 is the shared empty stub): it opens the block, writes the name of each sub unit definition in its list at +0x24 as a bare word, a space after each in a text save, **with no indent** - which is why a template's types sit at column 0 - and closes it. A template has no keys. Written under its name by CCountry::SaveContents' `saved_templates` loop. 0x57EFD0 to the `ret 4` at 0x57F09B.
addresses.evidence: Read whole: SaveBeginBlock, the loop over [edi+0x24] formatting definition+8 with '%s', the ' ' at 0x15B4E94 only where writer +0xC is clear, the open-coded close. The saves' templates read `GER_panzer_1936=` then `light_armor_brigade light_armor_brigade motorized_brigade` at column 0.

addresses.name: CDivisionTemplate::Load
addresses.comment: Slot 3, overriding CPersistent::Load: reads bare words until `}` or the end of input, looks each up in the sub unit database by name and appends a hit to the list at +0x24/+0x28/+0x2C; a word that is no sub unit type is dropped in silence. 0x57F0A0 to the `ret 4` at 0x57F2BE.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing: the token loop testing 4 and 0x13, the StringHashFind at 0x57F220 on the database fetched lazily (global 0x1A886F0), the 16-byte node append at 0x57F25B-0x57F299.

addresses.name: CUnit::HasDescendant
addresses.comment: Whether `unit` is anywhere below this one in the order of battle: walks children (+0x1E4), true at the first that is `unit` or has it below. Recursive. Its only other callers are the two save writers (CUnit::SaveContents at 0x5B87BE, CCountry::SaveContents at 0x4D14FA), which use it to write a carrying fleet in the place of a carried unit whose own subtree holds that fleet. 0x5D3660 to the `ret 4` at 0x5D3690 (a second at 0x5D3698).
addresses.evidence: Read whole; findRefs --callers 0x5D3660 gives 0x4D14FA, 0x5B87BE and itself at 0x5D367E. In no virtual table.

addresses.name: CUnit_SaveTokenForOobLevel
addresses.comment: The inverse of CUnit_OobLevelForToken: the unit's oob_level (+0x1F4) to its block key - 0 theatre (1125), 1 armygroup (1126), 2 army (592), 3 corps (1127), 4 division (1128), 5 navy (593), 6 air (1088), anything else `none` (397). Bare `ret`s. Callers: CUnitDeployment::SaveContents (0x57E3FC) and two in 0x5B9800-0x5B9850 not read.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x5B9650-0x5B9691, the table at 0x5B9694. findRefs --callers gives three sites.

addresses.name: SaveWriteIntList
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SaveWriteIntList(SaveToken key@ECX, CList<int>* list@EDX, CSaveWriter* writer@stack:4)
addresses.comment: A CList of ints as `key = { a b c }`: **nothing at all where the list's count (+8) is 0**; otherwise the key, a block, an indent, every value as `%d` with a space after it in a text save, and the close. The writer of a unit's `path`, a plan's `path` and `path2` and a brigade definition's `model`. Read back by ParseIntList. 0x40A810 to the `ret 4` at 0x40A98C.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing: the count test `cmp [edi+8], 0 / je` at 0x40A83B, SaveWriteKey, SaveBeginBlock, the loop with '%d' and ' '. CUnit::SaveContents calls it unconditionally for `path` and the census has `path` on only 2,717 of 14,007 unit blocks.

addresses.name: ParseIntList
addresses.comment: Reads a `{ a b c }` block of ints into a CList<int> - CUnit::LoadKey's `path` (into +0x138) and CBrigadeConstructionDefinition::LoadKey's `model`. 0x40A3C0 to the `ret 8` at 0x40A4BC. Whether it clears the list first was not read.
addresses.evidence: Likely: called with the parse context and the list pushed as its two stack arguments at 0x5B6F90-0x5B6F9B, `ret 8`; its body runs sscanf '%i' (0xB964D4) per token and allocates a node per value, read in outline only. Wrong if it stored into anything but the list given.

addresses.name: ParseLongFloat
addresses.comment: The reader of a 0x18F long_float - a 64-bit fixed point of 15 fractional bits - beside ParseFixedPoint: for the binary tokenizer, `sscanf(value, "%lld")`; for the text one, a token already typed 0x18F is taken whole, and anything else is converted from its decimal text by 0xA697F0. So `current_experience=2000.00000` comes back as 2000 << 15. Bare `ret`s. Callers: CLeader::LoadKey's `current_experience` (0x57FBF3) and two others at 0x42C2C0 and 0x45F237 not read.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0xA7B5A0-0xA7B636: the tokenizer slot 2 kind test, the '%lld' path, the `cmp [esi+0x228], 0x18F` arm and the 0xA697F0 arm, each storing two dwords at [edi]. The leader writer emits the same type, so the pair round-trips.

addresses.name: CCountry_CopyDefaultTemplates
addresses.comment: **Where every country gets its twelve templates**: frees the templates vector (+0x148/+0x14C), copies every template of the defaults vector at +0x138 into it, and then **pads it to 12** with empty templates named `PW_TEMPLATE_<index>` (the decimal position). Called by CCountry::LoadKey's `default_templates` case (0xCE134) right after the file's templates are read into +0x138. That is why every saved_templates block in a save has twelve entries, the last ones PW_TEMPLATE_n. 0x4D2740 to the `ret 4` at 0x4D2B53.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing for its shape: the delete loop over +0x148, the copy loop over +0x138/+0x13C allocating 0x34-byte templates, the `cmp eax, 0x30 / jge` bound at 0x4D293A and the only reference to the string `PW_TEMPLATE_` (0x15C0ED8) at 0x4D29B0 with itoa base 10. Census: 707 saved_templates blocks in seven saves, every one twelve entries long.

addresses.name: CCountry_LoadTemplates
addresses.comment: Reads a block of `<name> = { types }` entries into a vector of CDivisionTemplate*: each key becomes a new 0x34-byte template named by the key text, read by its slot 3 (CDivisionTemplate::Load) and pushed onto the vector. Used for `default_templates` into CCountry +0x138 and for `saved_templates` into +0x148 (which CCountry::LoadKey empties first, 0xCE158/0xCE15E). It does not pad, so a save's saved_templates stand as written. 0x503660 to the `ret 8` at 0x50389B.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing for its loop (token tests 4 and 0x13, operator_new 0x34, the template slot calls, VectorOfPointers_Reserve on growth); both callers push the vector and then the parse context.

addresses.name: AfterLoad_KeepLoadedId
addresses.comment: **A folded six-instruction AfterLoad**, slot 5 of CBuildingConstruction, CConvoyConstruction, CUnitDeployment, CBuildingDeployment and CConvoy: where the loaded id pair (+8/+0xC) is not 0/0, hand it to the object's slot 6 (CReferenceObject::SetId) to register it; otherwise nothing - unlike CUnit::AfterLoad and CMilitaryConstruction::AfterLoad it mints no id and does not move the counter. Bare `ret`. Named for no class because the body sits in three families' tables.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x57D270-0x57D287. vtable.py --holding 0x57D270: exactly those five tables at slot 5; CReferenceObject's own slot 5 is the empty stub 0xABF890, so the body is not inherited from it.

addresses.name: COrder::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall COrder::LoadKey(COrder* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **Nine keys, not eight**: `province` (atoi, then the province pointer from the game state's array at +0x2200, into +0xC), `target` (ParseObjectId into +0x10), `stance` (ParseInt into +0x20), `priority` (ParseInt into +0x1C), `stop` (ParseFixedPoint into +0x24), `start_date` (into +0x28) and **`death_date` (into +0x2C)**, both through Date_SetFromString, `time` (sscanf `%i` into +0x30) and `return_to_base` (ParseBool into +0x18). Anything else is dropped. The four tokens between 0x69 and 0x124 go through a byte table at 0x587134 and a jump table at 0x587120. Inherited by CNullOrder, CMoveOrder and CStrategicRedeploymentOrder, and the tail of every other order's loader. switchmap.py stops short of the death_date arm and reads two cases (`"` and `=`) out of the next function's bytes, which is why this was recorded with eight; the keys mirror COrder::SaveContents exactly.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing, 0x586FE0-0x58711D: `cmp eax, 0x358 / jg / je 0x5870F0` at 0x587089, and 0x5870F0 calls 0x44CDA0 with esi = this+0x2C. The two bogus cases resolve to 0x58723C and 0x5872FF, inside the function that starts at 0x5871F0. Every order block in the saves carries `death_date`.

addresses.name: CUnit::AfterLoad
addresses.comment: **CPersistent slot 5, and where a unit's id comes from**; `this` is the unit's CPersistent at +8, and the offsets below are the unit's own. If the block carried an id (either half of the pair at +0x10 non-zero) it registers it through slot 6 (SetId) and then pushes the global generator at 0x170AF78 past it, so a later runtime id cannot collide with it. If it carried none, it takes `counter++` and stamps id type **0x29 (41)**. That is why an OOB file need not carry ids at all, and why units from one that does not - the mod's flying_dutchman files - come out as type 41. **Then, only where the unit has a location (+0x130)**: CUnit::RebuildDefinition(unit, true), clears +0x48 (the byte every loader sets before reading a unit block), CUnit::RebuildAvatar, CUnit::EnterProvince(its location) a second time, and the primary slot 18 (CheckBase on a fleet or an air unit, the empty stub on a land unit). A unit with no location - the only kind is one in the deployment pool - gets the id and nothing else. Bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-oob.md.
addresses.evidence: Read whole, 0x5B80D0-0x5B8168: the id test at 0x5B80DC, slot 6 at 0x5B80EF, the counter at 0x5B80F8/0x5B8107, the location test `cmp [esi+0x128], 0` (unit +0x130), the calls 0x5B5ED0, 0x5BDC70, 0x5BEFD0 and slot 18 through [edx+0x48]. Slot 18 of CNavy and CAir is CheckBase, of CUnit and CArmy 0xABF890.

addresses.name: CUnit::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CUnit::LoadKey(CUnit* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment:
**The whole of what an order of battle block accepts** - a `division`, `corps`, `army`, `navy`, `air` or `theatre` - 40 keys in one switch of 4658 bytes. Seven open a child unit (`theatre`, `armygroup`, `army`, `corps`, `division`, `navy`, `air`), three say what the unit is made of (`regiment`, `ship`, `wing`, all reaching CSubUnit::LoadKey), four are identity (`id`, `name`, `location`, `leader`) and the rest is state a save carries: `path`, `track`, `previous`, `movement_progress`, `retreat`, `possible_retreat`, `disengage`, `arrow_state`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `was_paradropped`, `supplies`, `fuel`, `dig_in`, `attack_delay`, `combat_hours`, `can_upgrade`, `can_reinforce`, `is_reserve`, `is_prioritized`, `plan`, `expeditionary_owner`, `expeditionary_date`, `aggression_enabled`, `aggression_setting`, `country_intel`. The loader cannot tell an OOB file from a save - it is the same switch - so every one of them is legal in `history/units`.

**Any other key goes to CreateOrder** (the default at 0x5B7E3F): where the token is one of its 33 order kinds the new order reads the block (its slot 3) and becomes the unit's order (+0xB0), **without freeing an order already there**; anything else is dropped. That is how `strategic_redeployment`, `patrol`, `air_intercept` and the rest come back.

**A child unit**: a new CArmy (or CNavy, or CAir), +0x48 set, oob_level from the key, slot 28 with this unit's idler, the owner copied, the block read; **without a `location` it is deleted**; with one it is hung under this unit (CUnit_AttachToParent - for a land child only where this unit answers IsLand) and added to its owner's unit list. **A `regiment`, `ship` or `wing`**: a new sub unit with this unit's owner and unit_ptr (+0xB0) - a regiment also takes is_reserve where this unit's +0x96 is set, before and after its block - read, added with AddRegimentToUnit, and given a name where it has none: a ship or wing from CCountry::MakeSubUnitName, a regiment `<n>. <unit name>`. **`location`**: the province by id and CUnit::EnterProvince; outside a game loaded from a save (+0xD9C) an unknown id puts the unit in province 1 with an error and enemy ground or under 20% infrastructure only logs. The scalars land where CUnit::SaveContents reads them (`this` is the unit + 8): fixed through TokenToFixedPoint or ParseFixedPoint, `track`, `was_paradropped`, `is_prioritized`, `can_reinforce`, `can_upgrade`, `aggression_enabled` and `is_reserve` through ParseBool, `retreat` true only for the word yes, `start_date`/`end_date` through Date_SetFromString, `previous` as a province, `country_intel` as a vector re-cut into 12-byte grants.

**The keyword does not pick the class, the parent does**: CNavy::LoadKey and CAir::LoadKey take the five child-unit keywords back and send all five to one handler that still builds a CArmy. Reached from RTTI, not from the first vftable: CArmy keeps CPersistent at object offset 8, so slot 4 of its primary table is a per-unit update and not this. **`leader`** (token 0x268): a plain number is looked up as the persistent {id, type 0x25} across the whole game and put on with CUnit::SetLeader(leader, 0, 0) - no check of his country, rank or kind; a save's {id type} block goes through ParseObjectReference to the same setter. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: The default arm read whole at 0x5B7E3F-0x5B7E7E (CreateOrder(token, 0) with edi = unit, slot 3, the store at [ebx+0xA8] = unit +0xB0 with no release); the child arms 0x5B762B and 0x5B7A8B with the location test and 0x5B7B2B's delete; the regiment arm 0x5B7386-0x5B7520 and the ship and wing arms; the location arm 0x5B7012-0x5B7383 with the strings ' invalid location. Spawning at province ID=1.', ' at start, but that is enemy territory.' and ' at start, but that has less than 20% infra.'. Every key's store was matched against CUnit::SaveContents' read of the same offset.

addresses.name: CMilitaryConstruction::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CMilitaryConstruction::LoadKey(CMilitaryConstruction* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **The keys its switch names**, 8 of them, one case each: `accumulated_experiance`, `accumulated_progress`, `factor`, `is_reserve`, `manpower`, `name`, `target`, `unit`. **Any other key is first looked up as a sub unit type's name** (the database by StringHashFind): on a hit a new CBrigadeConstructionDefinition is made, its block read and appended to the brigade list at +0x7C/+0x80/+0x84 - which is how a save's `infantry_brigade = { id name model }` lines come back. Only a key that is no type goes to CConstruction::LoadKey for `id`, `cost`, `duration`, `progress`, `status`, `size`, `location`, `country` and `builder`; anything else is dropped there.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing, 0x4840C0-0x4843E4: the default at 0x48420D builds the key text, calls CSubUnitDataBase::GetInstance (0x5ADE80) and StringHashFind (0x9C7D60); a hit allocates and constructs (0x482AE0), calls slot 3 and links the node at +0x7C..+0x84; a miss reaches `call 0x483200` at 0x48434C. switchmap.py lists only the eight named cases.

addresses.name: CAir::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAir::LoadKey(CAir* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: What an `air` block adds over CUnit::LoadKey: `base`, and the land units it carries. `base` (0x509): atoi, the province by id, and CUnit::SetBase with that province's base object (+0x54) - **no test that the province has an air base**, where CNavy::LoadKey logs a missing naval base. The five child-unit keywords are taken back off the base and sent to one handler of its own, which builds a CArmy (byte +0x48 set, oob_level from the key, the owner copied, the block read) and, where it has a location, **puts it aboard with CAir::Board** and adds it to its owner's unit list - the reader of what CAir::SaveContents writes; without a location it is not kept. The four land keywords reach one body through a range test - `cmp eax, 0x465 / jl default / cmp eax, 0x468 / jg default` and fall through - which switchmap.py did not read until 2026-09-28, so this was recorded with four keys and not eight. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-oob.md.
addresses.evidence: The handler 0x5D0563-0x5D061F read: CUnit_OobLevelForToken, slot 28, CUnit_SetOwner, slot 3, the location test, CAir::Board (0x5D0920) with esi = this - 8, CCountry::AddUnit. The base arm 0x5D0665-0x5D06A3: atoi, [province+0x54], CUnit::SetBase.

addresses.name: CLeaderHistory::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Slot 2 of CLeaderHistory, CDiplomaticHistory and CWarHistory - the same body in all three, which is why it is recorded on one of them and the slot recorded on the other two. Walks the list at +0xC and, for each entry, asks **CHistoryEntry::DateIsUnset (0x1EC6E0)**: an unset date goes straight to the entry's own slot 2, and a real one is first formatted through 0x44C710 and opened as a `<date> = { ... }` block. `ret 4`. CCountryHistory and CProvinceHistory use a different and much larger writer at 0x1FCDA0. **A leader's history is not written into a save**: CLeader::SaveContents (0x17FDB0) writes rank, skill, current_experience, gainable_trait and trait and never calls its history, and none of the 24,441 active leader entries in seven saves has a `history` key - the leader's history comes back from history/leaders. Which writer reaches the CLeaderHistory table's copy of this slot, if any, was not found.
addresses.evidence: CLeader::SaveContents read whole (0x57FDB0-0x57FF59): its only slot call on a member is the tracker at +0xC4; the history at +0x84 is not touched. The seven-save census of active_leaders entries finds rank, skill, current_experience, gainable_trait and trait only. findRefs --callers 0x5F28E0 gives no direct call. Corrects the old comment's 'So a leader's history block is written back out whole on every save'.

struct_fields.name: loading
struct_fields.comment: Set to 1 on a new unit by every loader just before it reads the unit's block - CCountry::LoadKey's land, navy and air cases (0x4CD994, 0x4CD272, 0x4CDA40), CUnit::LoadKey's child cases (0x5B7AC6, 0x5B7663) and CAir::LoadKey's land handler (0x5D0592) - and cleared by CUnit::AfterLoad (0x5B8143) where the unit has a location. What reads it was not surveyed, so the name rests on its writers.
struct_fields.evidence: Inferred: the six `mov byte ptr [esi+0x48], 1` / `[edi+0x48], 1` stores, each on the primary pointer of a just-constructed unit before its slot 3; the clear `mov byte ptr [esi+0x40], 0` in AfterLoad where esi is the unit + 8. Wrong if a reader used it for something other than the load window.

struct_fields.name: saved_this_pass
struct_fields.comment: **The unit has been written in this save.** CCountry::SaveContents clears it on every unit of the country (0x4D137A) before writing them; CUnit::SaveContents sets it as it starts (0x5B819F); and CUnit::SaveContents' child loop skips a child that already has it (0x5B8656) - so a unit written once, for instance a fleet written in the place of the unit it carries, is not written again under its own parent.
struct_fields.evidence: The three sites read on the listing: `mov byte ptr [ecx+0x49], 0` in the loop over CCountry +0xBAC, `mov byte ptr [ebx+0x41], 1` with ebx = unit + 8, `cmp byte ptr [esi+0x49], 0 / jne skip` on the child. Wrong if anything else wrote the byte between those.

struct_fields.name: upgrading_from_strength
struct_fields.comment: Thousandths, saved as `upgrading_from_subunit_str` beside `upgrading_from_subunit` (+0x38) - written only where not 0 and read back with TokenToFixedPoint. Presumably the strength of the brigade being upgraded; what uses it was not read.
struct_fields.evidence: Writer: CBrigadeConstructionDefinition::SaveContents, `mov esi,[esi+0x3C]` then SaveWriteFixed(0x7CF) at 0x4830FB-0x48310C. Loader: the 0x7CF case at 0x482ED2 stores TokenToFixedPoint's answer at [ebx+0x3C]. The meaning is inferred from the key name only.

slots_noted: One body here is named for no class on purpose: 0x17D270 (AfterLoad_KeepLoadedId) is a six-instruction AfterLoad the linker folded across five tables in three families - CBuildingConstruction, CConvoyConstruction, CUnitDeployment, CBuildingDeployment and CConvoy, each at slot 5, all recorded above - and CReferenceObject's own slot 5 is the empty stub, so no class owns it. Every other function in this file has its slot recorded under each table that holds it.
